query: What are the six failure modes that usually stall Kyriba rollouts, and how should AbarVa de-risk them for Lakeshore?
answer: For Lakeshore, the Kyriba risks are very standard — and all six are fixable if you design for them up front. My read, grounded in what’s working/going-wrong at other large holdcos: 1) Fuzzy scope between “treasury platform” and “ERP/finance plumbing” Failure mode: Kyriba gets blamed for gaps that actually sit in ERP, bank connectivity, or TMS-adjacent workflows (cash app, intercompany, In-House Bank). Projects stall while teams argue “who owns what.” De‑risk move: – Make a one-page RACI on “Kyriba vs ERP vs banks vs data lake” and have Treasury, Corporate Finance, and CIO sign it. – In AbarVa: codify this as an explicit scope/RACI artifact in the Move, and wire a gate — project can’t advance to build until all three functions e‑sign that artifact. 2) Bank connectivity complexity underestimated Failure mode: Timelines assume “Kyriba connects to banks,” but file formats, onboarding queues, and security reviews add months. Rollouts slip; Treasury starts doing dual work in Excel and legacy tools. De‑risk move: – Build a bank-by-bank connectivity matrix (protocols, file types, lead times, security hoops) as a formal deliverable. – In AbarVa: treat each critical bank connection as its own mini-milestone with risk scoring; surface any that haven’t cleared InfoSec / vendor-security review as a red flag at steering.
